title: Creamy White Bean & Cabbage Soup
description: A cozy inexpensive soup with tender cabbage and creamy white beans.

ingredients.item: white beans, drained, 14 to 15 ounces each

substitutions: Use chickpeas instead of white beans.
Skip the milk for a brothy version.

steps.text: Cook onion and cabbage until beginning to soften.
Add beans, broth, and thyme; simmer until cabbage is tender.
Mash some beans and stir in milk if using.

cookSteps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon oil or butter in a large pot. Add 1 diced small onion and cook 4 minutes.
Add 4 cups sliced cabbage and cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add 2 cans drained white beans, 4 cups broth, and 1/2 teaspoon thyme. Simmer 15 minutes until the cabbage is tender.
Mash some of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the soup. Stir in 1/2 cup milk or half-and-half if using and warm through.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 2 months.

title: Sheet-Pan Lemon Chickpeas & Broccoli
description: A simple sheet-pan dinner with crisp chickpeas, roasted broccoli, and bright lemon.
substitutions: Use cauliflower for part or all of the broccoli.
Serve over rice or couscous for a larger meal.

steps.text: Heat oven and season chickpeas and broccoli.
Roast until broccoli browns and chickpeas are crisp.

cookSteps.text: Heat oven to 425°F. Put 2 cans dried chickpeas and 5 cups broccoli florets on a sheet pan.
Toss with 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Roast 22–25 minutes, stirring once, until the broccoli edges are browned and the chickpeas are lightly crisp.
Squeeze the juice of 1 lemon over the hot pan and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days; reheat uncovered for best texture.

title: Leftover Rice Breakfast Bowl
description: A fast savory breakfast that turns cold leftover rice into a warm egg bowl.

steps.text: Cook the egg in the same skillet.

cookSteps.text: Heat 1 teaspoon butter or oil in a skillet. Add 1 cup cold cooked rice and stir 3–4 minutes until hot.
Push the rice to one side. Crack in 1 egg and cook to your preferred doneness, about 2–3 minutes.
Drizzle the rice with 1 teaspoon soy sauce. Add 2 tablespoons cheese or scallions if using, and serve the egg over the rice.

title: Small-Batch Peach Crisp
description: A warm two-serving fruit crisp with an oat-brown-sugar topping.

ingredients.item: sliced peaches, fresh or thawed frozen

substitutions: Use apples, pears, or berries instead of peaches.

steps.text: Heat oven and fill a small dish with seasoned peaches.
Mix and add the oat topping.

cookSteps.text: Heat oven to 375°F. Put 2 cups sliced peaches in a small baking dish and toss with 1 tablespoon brown sugar and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon.
Mix 1/4 cup oats, 2 tablespoons flour, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, and 2 tablespoons softened butter until crumbly. Sprinkle over the peaches.
Bake 22–25 minutes until the fruit bubbles and the topping is golden.
